why: ONE file holds every sound number of a project, each with its reason. Docs and briefs name the key, code reads the key. A number changes only by an edit here with the measurement that justifies it; a check limit is never loosened to pass. Values below are the calibration project's of 2026-10-26. voice_edges.py reads take.edge + checks.edge_noise; voice_measure.py reads checks.refq + checks.takeq.

voice.lufs_target_why: per-take gated loudness before the bus: narrator and characters at one level
voice.highpass_why: 70 for a deep male narrator (a male F0 reaches 85 Hz; 90 Hz at 12 dB/oct takes 3 dB of it)
voice.eq_why: [hz, q, gain]: cut boxy low mids, lift presence so consonants read on a phone
voice.deess_why: de-ess only a take whose sibilant band comes within this of its speech band; on every take it dulls

edge.why: guards keep a soft onset and the decay of a final consonant; fades sit inside the guards only. Every other edge key defaults to voice_edges.DEFAULT_EDGE

gen_cap.why: cap = tokens_per_s x (base_s + letters / (slowest / margin)); measured per voice AND reference clip

eos.why: force end-of-speech 1.2 s after the engine marks the text complete (6x Chatterbox's own 200 ms long-tail rule)

edge_noise.why: VOICE-EDGE-NOISE: noise-only sound allowed beyond the guards

refq.why: REF-QUALITY, calibrated on clips the owner approved vs rejected by ear (calibration project 2026-10-24/25)

master.why: aim under the delivery ceiling so the AAC encode has headroom

delivery.why: measured on the delivered AAC, not the WAV. A platform with no sourced number is reported as a gap, never guessed

silence.why: no dead hole; pauses carry bed or room, never digital zero
